recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一個巨大多核細胞，六、七個分開的圓形至橢圓形細胞核，各自帶有小核仁，散布在大量淡藍灰色、細顆粒狀的細胞質中，這是蝕骨細胞（osteoclast）而非核葉相連的巨核細胞。
features: Very large multinucleated cell, many times the diameter of surrounding cells
Multiple (about 6-7) separate, round to oval nuclei of similar size, not overlapping or lobulated
Nuclei with finely granular chromatin and small single nucleoli
Abundant, irregularly shaped, pale blue-gray cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granularity and frayed edges
Background of normal marrow elements: erythroid precursors, granulocytes, and lymphocytes
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a very large multinucleated cell with abundant, finely granular, pale blue-gray cytoplasm and irregular, frayed borders. It contains multiple discrete round to oval nuclei of uniform size, each with fine chromatin and a small nucleolus, without nuclear lobation or overlap. Surrounding hematopoietic cells, including erythroid precursors and granulocytes, appear unremarkable. Findings are consistent with an osteoclast, a normal marrow constituent more often seen in aspirates from children or states of increased bone remodeling.

ddx.vs: A megakaryocyte has a single multilobated, interconnected nucleus with dense chromatin and pink granular cytoplasm, whereas the osteoclast has multiple separate, uniform nuclei with nucleoli.
Tumor clusters show cohesive, pleomorphic, overlapping nuclei with distinct cell borders, whereas the osteoclast has uniform bland nuclei in one shared cytoplasm.
Osteoblasts are mononuclear with an eccentric nucleus and a paranuclear hof, often in small clusters, unlike the multinucleated osteoclast.
Histiocytic giant cells arise in granulomas with epithelioid histiocytes and inflammation, while an isolated osteoclast in an otherwise normal aspirate lacks that setting.
